era: Background: Peña, Ueno and the Central Bank (2023–2025)

events.title: Santiago Peña takes office for a five-year term
events.detail: Peña, of the Colorado Party and mentored by ex-president Horacio Cartes, became president in August 2023 with Pedro Alliana as vice president. His term was due to run to August 2028. Suspicions about his ties to the Ueno group are reported to date from around this time.

events.title: Former Ueno head Carlos Carvallo appointed to lead the Central Bank
events.detail: RPP dates the appointment to September 2023. Carlos Carvallo Spalding had led Financiera Ueno, from which the later bank originated. The impeachment accusation says the BCP board authorised the operation 83 days after his appointment. The appointment drew conflict-of-interest criticism.

events.title: Ueno becomes a bank with over 500,000 clients
events.detail: La República reports Ueno had more than 500,000 clients when it became a bank in late 2023. By September 2026 the figure exceeded 3 million.

events.title: Peña sells his shares in Grupo Vázquez / Ueno Holding
events.detail: RPP dates the sale to March 2025 and Infobae/EFE to April 2025; the sources differ on the month. Peña had been a business partner of the group until then, which underpins the conflict-of-interest charge. The bank has said he was never a shareholder or investor, so this is contested.

events.title: Central Bank warns of excess lending to owner-linked firms
events.detail: RPP reports the BCP warned that Ueno was granting too many loans to companies linked to its owners. The year is not stated in the article and is inferred as 2026.

events.title: Public entities hold about a quarter of Ueno deposits
events.detail: RPP reports state bodies and funds injected capital into Ueno until they made up about a quarter of its deposits. The state pension and health fund IPS held roughly $355–380 million (Infobae/EFE: about 9% of IPS investments).

events.title: Central Bank board votes to put Ueno into resolution
events.detail: CNN and RPP report the BCP board unanimously voted to start resolution after Ueno's solvency ratio fell below half the legal minimum. Infobae/EFE dates the order to Tuesday 3 November, so the exact day varies by source. Around 3 million people, about 60% of Paraguayan adults, were locked out of their savings.

events.title: Carvallo resigns; prosecutors order arrest of ten Ueno executives
events.detail: Carlos Carvallo resigned from the Central Bank. Prosecutors ordered the arrest of ten Ueno executives, and depositors began protesting outside closed branches.

events.title: Peña promulgates fast-track depositor repayment law
events.detail: Congress passed the law in record time and Peña signed it. Each depositor can receive up to 40 monthly minimum wages (121.7 million guaraníes, about $20,000) within 24 hours and no later than five business days, per CNN. An impeachment request against Peña and Alliana was also filed on 4 November.

events.title: Deputies open impeachment debate under Article 225
events.detail: The Chamber began debating at 10:38 local time on an accusation backed by 35 opposition and dissident Colorado legislators, citing grave and systematic misconduct. Charges include conflict of interest, undue interference at IPS, and two simultaneous Ueno loans to Peña. Passage needed two-thirds. Horacio Cartes said the Colorado Party would back the motion.

events.title: Peña announces resignation in a video; Congress never accepts it
events.detail: Peña posted a video saying he resigned for the country's stability and to avoid further harm. The session convened to consider the resignation lacked quorum, so it was neither accepted nor rejected and he stayed formally president.

events.title: Deputies approve the accusation; Alliana's impeachment rejected
events.detail: La Nación reports 78 legislators present approved the accusation, including all Colorado members, while deputies declined to open proceedings against Vice President Pedro Alliana. One outlet gave a different tally (48 against, 30 in favor) that appears to concern Alliana; treat counts with caution.

events.title: Judge orders pretrial detention of Ueno executives
events.detail: Judge Rodrigo Estigarribia ordered six executives, including president Juan Manuel Gustale and executive director Federico Vázquez Villasanti, into pretrial detention, and two others under house arrest. 27 people had been prosecuted for breach of trust, attempted fraud and related offenses.

events.title: Senate rejects 72-hour delay and removes Peña, 44 votes to 0
events.detail: The Senate began about 10:43. It rejected Peña's request for 72 more hours (39 against, 2 abstentions), admitted the evidence 41-0, and removed him at about 22:04 for mal desempeño, with 44 in favor and one absent. Senate president Basilio Núñez announced the result.

events.title: Pedro Alliana assumes the presidency until August 2028
events.detail: Under Article 234 of the Constitution the vice president takes over. La Nación puts the formal assumption at 22:51 on 6 November.

events.title: Peña reported detained under house arrest after removal
events.detail: La Nación's live blog reports prosecutors ordered house arrest at about 22:42 and that he was taken to the Regimiento Escolta Presidencial, on charges of breach of trust, influence peddling and administration for personal benefit. Protesters clashed with police at his home. The other outlets reviewed do not confirm the arrest, and the blog is internally inconsistent on timing.
events.confidenceReason: Single live-blog source; other outlets do not confirm.
